title: LeBron James Takes His Time Picking His Next Team
summary:
Have you ever had to make a really big choice, like which summer camp to go to or what pet to get? Now imagine that choice is watched by millions of people and could change the whole sport of basketball. That's what LeBron James is going through right now!

LeBron, who is 41 years old, is one of the greatest basketball players of all time. He's played 22 All-Star games—more than anyone else! Three weeks ago, he told the Los Angeles Lakers that he would not come back for his 24th season. Now, he's a free agent, which means any team can try to sign him.

His agent, Rich Paul, said on a podcast that LeBron is not in a hurry. "We're not going to be rushed," Paul said. "It's his choice to make, and when he makes the choice, he'll make it." He also said teams don't need to give them any more information. They already understand everything.

So where might LeBron go? Reports say he could join the Golden State Warriors, the Philadelphia 76ers, or return to the Miami Heat or Cleveland Cavaliers. But Paul insists this isn't like 2010, when LeBron had a TV show called "The Decision" to announce he was leaving Cleveland for Miami. That was a huge spectacle. This time, Paul says, "We're not making this about attention and a spectacle." It's a business choice.

Even the NBA commissioner, Adam Silver, is eager. He joked he wants LeBron "to make his announcement already, so we can finish the schedule." But LeBron is taking his time. Last season, he averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists, and 6.1 rebounds per game. Over his career, he's played a record 1,622 games. Wherever he goes, fans will be watching!
why_it_matters: Like choosing a summer camp or team, LeBron shows that big decisions need careful thought, especially when everyone is watching.

This time, LeBron and his agent want the process to be quieter and more about the basketball choice.
Free agency happens every year, letting players switch teams after their contract ends.
